# Allowed counts by context
#
# Polars: the release py-2.2.0 at the commit 08b2814ce6386c0efe0fea512912353f42a8b7b6 of vendor/polars.
# Generated from the catalogue and Polars by the engine test
# `allowed::tests::artifacts::the_committed_tables_are_what_polars_gives`, with Polars on
# one thread, so that a reason that depends on which of two failures comes first is the
# same every time, in the Cargo profile `measure`, which builds Polars as its release
# does: optimised, without debug assertions or overflow checks. Do not edit.
# To refresh after a change of the catalogue or of Polars:
#   DAGEIST_REFRESH_TABLES=1 cargo test --offline --locked --profile measure -p dageist-engine \
#     allowed::tests::artifacts
# See docs/how-to.md, "Refresh The Tables Of Allowed Combinations".
#
# Each line is: context | count | outcome.
#
# The context table measures each entry as it gives its values. How many values a chain
# gives is not an entry's alone, for a method that follows a count keeps it, so this table
# measures the counts: a chain that ends in a context and gives one value, as many values
# as the table has rows, or another number of them, which the data or the arguments
# decide. The columns hold three rows, and the other number is the first two of them.
# Where the place needs a `Boolean`, the values are those of a `Boolean` column; in a
# join key the other table's key has the dtype the key has; and in a pivot's aggregate
# they are the values of a group.
#
# The outcome is `allowed -`, or `refused <stage>: <Polars' reason>`.
#
# An outcome is `allowed <dtype of the result> <one|many>` (`-` for a step), or
# `refused <stage>: <Polars' reason>`. A combination is allowed only when Polars resolved
# its schema, ran it on three rows that include a null, and ran it on a table with no rows.
# The stage is where Polars refused it: `schema`; `rows`, when the schema resolved and
# the rows were refused; or `empty`, when only the table with no rows was. `one` is a
# value for the three rows together, `many` any other number. A reason is Polars' message
# up to its first blank line, on one line.
#
# 135 combinations: 82 allowed; 18 refused when Polars resolved the schema, 35 when it ran the rows, 0 when it ran the empty table.
#

aggregate > condition.predicate | one | allowed -
